name: Lunazul

facts.base: 100% blue Weber agave, grown on the estate and harvested by hand
facts.age: Varies: the blanco is unaged; the reposado rests at least two months
facts.cask: Reposado and añejo rest in barrels that once held bourbon; the blanco sees no wood
facts.law: Tequila under Mexico's denomination of origin: blue agave from Jalisco and parts of four states; 100% agave on the label

made: Lunazul is made at the Tierra de Agaves distillery in the heart of the tequila country of Jalisco, from 100 per cent blue Weber agave grown on the estate and harvested by hand, then distilled and bottled there. The blanco is bottled unaged; the reposado rests at least two months, and the añejo at least a year, in barrels that once held bourbon. Each is bottled at 40 per cent. The label here shows the name and 100%, not the expression.
taste: The blanco: cooked agave, honey and herbs on the nose, then zesty lime and black pepper, with a creamy finish. The reposado: the same agave softened by vanilla and light oak from the bourbon barrels, warm and peppery at the end.

lines.s10: Lunazul is a Jalisco tequila of 100 per cent blue agave, estate grown and distilled at the Tierra de Agaves distillery.
lines.s20: Lunazul, blue moon in Spanish, is tequila of 100 per cent blue agave, grown, distilled and bottled on one estate in Jalisco. The blanco is bright with lime and pepper; the reposado rests in old bourbon barrels for vanilla and a softer finish.
lines.s45: This is Lunazul, tequila of 100 per cent blue Weber agave, grown on the estate, harvested by hand, then distilled and bottled at the Tierra de Agaves distillery in the heart of the tequila country of Jalisco. The blanco goes into the bottle unaged; the reposado rests at least two months in barrels that once held bourbon. The blanco tastes of cooked agave and honey, then lime and black pepper with a creamy finish; the reposado adds vanilla and soft oak. We pour it in a Margarita or a Paloma, or neat with lime. Its name is Spanish for blue moon, and its black label is its mark.
lines.sale: Lunazul is an estate grown Jalisco tequila of 100 per cent blue agave, cooked agave and black pepper in the glass. It makes a clean, lively Margarita or Paloma.

serve.neat: Neat, about an ounce and a half, at room temperature, with a wedge of lime if asked.
serve.rocks: Over ice with lime, or long with grapefruit soda in a Paloma.
serve.glass: A rocks glass, a coupe for the Margarita, a highball for the Paloma.
serve.classic: The Margarita and the Paloma; also a Ranch Water, tequila with lime and soda.

guest: Lunazul is a Jalisco tequila of 100 per cent blue agave, grown and distilled on one estate: cooked agave and pepper, bright when unaged and softer with vanilla when rested, and made for a Margarita or a Paloma.
story: Lunazul is Spanish for blue moon, the two words luna and azul run together. The tequila is grown, distilled and bottled on one estate, the Tierra de Agaves distillery, in the heart of the tequila country of Jalisco, from blue agave harvested by hand. Its mark is the black label, kept when the bottle was redesigned in 2015, when a wolf was blown into the glass and the bottle took a cork stopper.
watch: Which expression is open decides the description: the blanco is clear and unaged; the reposado is pale gold from its bourbon barrels.
Blanco, silver and plata are one style, unaged: a guest who asks for a silver tequila can be offered the blanco.
Say it loo-nah-SOOL: luna azul, blue moon, run together into one word.
asks: Confirm at lineup that the black-labelled bottle in the tequila front row is Lunazul, and which expression it is.

recall.prompt: What is Lunazul, and how do its blanco and reposado differ?
recall.answer: A Jalisco tequila of 100 per cent blue Weber agave, estate grown, distilled and bottled at the Tierra de Agaves distillery, at 40% ABV. The blanco is unaged, bright with lime and pepper; the reposado rests at least two months in barrels that once held bourbon, for vanilla and softness.

quiz.q: What does the name Lunazul mean in Spanish?
quiz.explain: Blue moon: luna and azul run together. The wolf is blown into the glass of the bottle.

quiz.q: In what kind of barrel does Lunazul Reposado rest?
quiz.explain: Barrels that once held bourbon, which give the reposado its vanilla and soft oak; the blanco sees no wood.

quiz.q: How long, at least, does Lunazul Reposado rest in wood?
quiz.explain: At least two months, the reposado rule; an añejo needs at least a year.
